In Fleming County Schools, we believe students deepen their understanding when they do the thinking, connect ideas across subjects, and apply what they know to real problems. We work with families, community members, and local employers to design challenges that matter to students and to Fleming County. Through these experiences, students build the knowledge, skills, and confidence to contribute to their community and compete globally.

In Fleming County Schools, we believe students should have a real say in what they explore, how they approach their work, and how they show what they know. When students bring their interests, strengths, talents, cultural knowledge, and lived experiences to their work, they help shape what happens in the classroom and take greater ownership of their learning.

In Fleming County Schools, we believe every student deserves meaningful opportunities to show what they know and can do through writing, performances, projects, portfolios, and presentations. Above all, their work should provide clear evidence of grade-level and real-world readiness by showing how well they apply the knowledge and skills expected at their grade level to solve problems, make decisions, and communicate their thinking in authentic situations. Their work should also reflect who they are, what interests them, and what they aspire to do.

In Fleming County Schools, we believe students should receive feedback tied to clear expectations for mastery while they still have time to act on it. Students use Proficiency Scales to study examples, recognize what quality work looks like, and check their own work in progress. With timely feedback, they can see where they stand, decide what to improve, and take ownership of their next step.
Support to Take the Next Step

In Fleming County Schools, we believe every student deserves access to challenging grade-level learning and just-in-time support when they need it. Effective support helps students work through difficulty, do the thinking themselves, and take their next step with greater independence.

In Fleming County Schools, we believe every student can grow from where they are, master important knowledge and skills, build readiness for the next grade and life beyond school, and develop the agency to shape their own learning and future. Thriving also means feeling a sense of belonging, knowing yourself, developing socially and emotionally, and building habits that support physical health.
